text:
Jess: FYI opened PR 482 to tidy the 'evidence export' examples — there's a sticky sentence about how we describe exported audit events. PTAL Lina/Omar/Raj.
Lina: on it. can you paste the exact line? I skimmed but didn't catch this morning.
Jess: line in question: "Redwood stores tenant-scoped audit events for compliance purposes." Legal flagged 'stores' as ambiguous vs 'exports' in the SOC2 narrative.
Omar: yeah we should avoid 'stores' — implies indefinite retention. Suggest: "Redwood retains audit event records in accordance with configured customer retention policies and export procedures." shorter: "Retained per customer-configured retention policies."
Raj: +1 to avoiding 'stores'. also the SDK snippet in the PR uses Authorization: Bearer <key> but the curl example left out Content-Type and a sample query param. I can drop a corrected snippet.
Jess: please do. current snippet:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports" -d '{"scope":"tenant"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```
Lina: propose this instead (adds headers, example params, and deid flag):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports?format=jsonl&deidentify=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"tenant","start_time":"2025-02-01T00:00:00Z","end_time":"2025-02-28T23:59:59Z"}'
```
Raj: and python example too — small bug: they used requests.post(url, json=payload, headers) but didn't set timeout. add timeout in examples to encourage safe defaults.
Omar: on the compliance wording: Legal prefers we include the phrase "subject to customer-configured retention and redaction settings" when we mention exports. That covers legal-hold edgecases.
Jess: good call. I'll reword the paragraph: "Audit event exports are produced subject to customer-configured retention and redaction settings; consult your retention policy for export availability."
Lina: also suggested adding a short pseudonymization example for customers who want to share exports with third parties — quick snippet using our deidentify flag + mapping note.
Raj: can we add an inline note about filling PII placeholders? e.g. "when deidentify=true, fields matching PII patterns will be pseudonymized (sha256 prefix). Not reversible by Redwood."
Omar: Legal asked we avoid saying 'not reversible' as absolute. Change to: "pseudonymized (one-way hash with salt managed by the customer)"? But we don't expose salt. Maybe: "pseudonymized using a non-reversible transform. See cryptography section."
Jess: ok let's use: "pseudonymized using a one-way transform; see 'Export pseudonymization' in the cryptographic controls doc."
Lina: small editorial: re: example filenames — docs used export-<tenant>-<ts>.jsonl, legal prefers including retention policy id: export-<tenant>-<policyid>-<ts>.jsonl
Raj: I'll add that and link the retention policy API reference.
Jess: next steps: Lina to push snippet fixes -> Raj to run a quick linter on code block formatting -> Omar to confirm final compliance phrasing -> I'll merge once docs-bot confirms CI.
Lina: pushed a new commit addressing headers, deid flag, python timeout, and example filename.
docs-bot: CI passed for docs PR #482 (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482)
Omar: phrasing LGTM from security/compliance side. thanks everyone.
Jess: merging shortly. thanks for the quick turn around :tada: 
Lina: one follow-up — should we add a tiny integration test that asserts the example curl returns 202 in our docs test harness? I can add if we want a safety net.
Raj: +1, catches regressions when snippets get reordered.
docs-bot: docs PR #482 merged and deployed to staging (https://docs.staging.redwood.ai/exports).
